title: Reverse Alternating K-Node Groups
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list and a positive integer `k`, partition the list into consecutive groups of `k` nodes (the final group may have fewer than `k` nodes).

Numbering the groups `1, 2, 3, ...`, **reverse every odd-numbered group** (groups `1, 3, 5, ...` — including a trailing partial group if it falls on an odd group number) and **leave every even-numbered group** (`2, 4, 6, ...`) in its original order. Return the head of the modified list in `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 5000].
hints: Toggle a boolean flag `shouldReverse` (starting `true`) after each group of up to `k` nodes.
When `shouldReverse` is true, reverse up to `k` nodes in-place and connect the previous tail to the reversed group's new head; when false, simply advance `prev` up to `k` steps.

examples.explanation: Group 1 [1, 2, 3] reverses to [3, 2, 1], group 2 [4, 5, 6] stays [4, 5, 6], and partial odd group 3 [7, 8] reverses to [8, 7].
With k = 2, group 1 [1, 2] -> [2, 1], group 2 [3, 4] stays, group 3 [5, 6] -> [6, 5], group 4 [7] stays.
With k = 1, every group has length 1 so the list is unchanged.
